errors.description: Model incorrectly inferred that the last shape in the sequence (white) took the longest time to reach, conflating sequence position with duration. The ground truth explicitly states that the longest duration (2.00s) occurred when moving FROM white TO blue — meaning blue was the shape that took the longest time to reach FROM the previous shape (white). The model misattributes the duration to the starting point of the longest segment rather than the endpoint.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'The arrow takes the longest time to reach the white square because it is the last shape in the sequence.'

analysis_result.analysis: The model correctly identified the sequence of shapes and the final shape (white), but failed to interpret the question correctly. The question asks which shape took the longest time to reach FROM the previous shape — meaning, which destination shape had the longest inbound travel time. The ground truth shows the longest segment (2.00s) ends at the blue shape, not the white. The model’s reasoning erroneously assumes that being last in sequence implies longest duration, which is a logical fallacy. This is a textual logic error in reasoning, not a perception or grounding failure — the model had all correct data but drew an incorrect conclusion.
